local_patches.summary: Calc-translation hotfixes (PR #508 speed-program batch, live-verified bugs), STILL unlanded upstream as of source_commit d839036 — re-applied on top of this re-vendor rather than dropped. The prior local_patches entry for the v5.5/v5.6 field fixes (#414, commit d8a049a) is RETIRED here: diffing a from-scratch build of the previous source_commit (d769bec) against the previously-shipped bundle showed zero delta for warehouseDbSchemaFromConn/controlId-dedupe/resetIds/multiDsChild/memberAliases — that patch was already folded into upstream tableau.ts by the time d769bec was vendored (PR #107's 'upstream v5.5/v5.6 port'), so the entry was stale bookkeeping, not a live gap.
changes: ZN → native Sigma Zn() via TABLEAU_FUNC_MAP name-map; removed the single-paren Coalesce($1, 0) regex that emitted malformed Coalesce(Sum([x], 0)) for ZN(AGG(...)) — the dominant field null-guard idiom. NOTE: upstream d839036 still ships its OWN ZN → Coalesce($1, 0) behavior (see its new tableau.formula-literal-masking.test.ts assertion 'ZN([X]) -> Coalesce([X], 0)') — this patch supersedes that upstream default with the previously-verified native-Zn() behavior, same as before re-vendoring.

removed Coalesce from _TEXT_FN_RE: its type follows its args, and counting it as text-producing turned numeric ZN(a)+ZN(b) addition into silent string concat (&); _isTextOperand instead recurses into Coalesce's top-level args, so string-literal guard chains (Coalesce([a], "x") + …) still convert + to & while numeric or unknown-type guards keep +

start-of-week literal handling: DATETRUNC 3rd arg / 4-arg DATEDIFF 'monday' is still dropped (Sigma has no start-of-week slot) but now emits a verify warning instead of silent week-boundary drift; the drop is scoped to DateTrunc/DateDiff via a balanced-paren walk so other calls keeping a weekday string as a real last argument (e.g. CONTAINS(x, 'monday')) are no longer mangled. RE-PORTED THIS RE-VENDOR: upstream's own PR #118 (string-literal masking) rewrote this exact region from raw-quote regex matching to sentinel-based matching (literals are masked to ' <index>' tokens before this pass runs) — the old patch's context no longer matched (this was the only local_patches hunk of 36 that a mechanical diff-replay couldn't apply), so the balanced-paren walk was re-implemented against the masked string (`whole`/`off` from the replace callback) instead of the raw string. Same behavior, ported onto the new masked-text architecture; verified live (DATETRUNC('week', d, 'monday') still warns-and-drops, CONTAINS([Day], 'monday') is untouched).

stopped emitting non-existent Sigma functions: DATETIME → Date (was Datetime), DATEPART('weekday'/'dayofweek') → Weekday(date) with a numbering-verify warning (was DayOfWeek), DATENAME('week') → Text(DatePart("week", …)) at the source branch (was Text(Week(…)))

un-staled the window-untranslatable list: WINDOW_CORR/WINDOW_VAR/WINDOW_COUNT now map to MovingCorr/MovingVariance/MovingCount (offset forms spanning the current row; all three present in the Sigma function index, verified 2026-07-25); population variants WINDOW_VARP/COVARP/STDEVP stay untranslatable; SIGMA_CHART_ONLY_WINDOW_RE extended with MovingVariance/MovingCorr so the DM router keeps refusing them

local_patches.summary: Object-graph relationship key derivation ladder + coverage ledger (PR2a, bead beads-sigma-ovy4), STILL unlanded upstream as of source_commit d839036 (src/tableau.ts has zero diff between the prior source_commit d769bec and d839036 — confirmed via `git diff --stat d769bec..d839036 -- src/tableau.ts`, empty) — re-applied on top of this re-vendor by mechanical diff-replay (see local_patches note on the sibling entry above for method) rather than dropped. Unchanged from the prior vendoring; reproduced here verbatim for the record.
changes: object-graph relationship loop (relType === "collection"): the auto-match branch (previously an unconditional `continue` when the relationship carried zero serialized equality expressions) now first attempts conservative name-match inference — candidate column names are the normalized (whitespace-to-underscore, uppercased) display names already present on BOTH elements' colIdMap (existence tested via ensureCol's own bare lookup, never via a mutating call), filtered to key-shaped names by isKeyShapedName (see the dedicated bullet below for its exact, review-tightened rule). A single key-shaped candidate is wired with derivedVia: "name-inference"; ensureCol is only ever called on a name already confirmed to exist on both sides, so inference can fabricate neither a column nor a value. More than one key-shaped candidate, or none, leaves the relationship unwired — never a guessed composite key

entityNameOf(cleanName) — the 'target element's entity name' used by the key-shaped filter above: uppercases the target element's cleanName, then strips exactly one leading prefix matching /^(DIM|FACT|BRIDGE)_/ (so 'DIM_CUSTOMER' -> 'CUSTOMER', 'FACT_WIDE' -> 'WIDE', 'BRIDGE_ACCOUNT_USER' -> 'ACCOUNT_USER'; a cleanName with none of those three prefixes, e.g. 'CUSTOMER', passes through unchanged). The prefix match is effectively case-insensitive end-to-end because cleanName is uppercased before the regex runs (so 'dim_customer' or 'Dim_Customer' both strip to 'CUSTOMER' too) — only that single fixed 3-name prefix list is recognized; any other table-naming convention (no prefix, or a prefix outside DIM/FACT/BRIDGE) falls back to matching the full cleanName as the entity name, which may under-match the _ID/_KEY/_SK/_CODE suffix leg's sibling checks on real-world schemas that use different prefixing

isKeyShapedName(name, entityName) is `/_(ID|KEY|SK|CODE)$/.test(name) || !!entityName && (name === entityName || new RegExp('^' + escapeRe(entityName) + '_(ID|KEY|SK|CODE)$').test(name))` — three precise forms only: an explicit key suffix (entity-agnostic: two unrelated *_ID columns shared between two tables still correctly yield 2 candidates and no guess, by design), the entity name exactly, or the entity name plus a key suffix. A new escapeRe(s) helper (regex-metacharacter escaping) guards the third form so an entity name is never interpolated into a RegExp unescaped. Verified against all four review scenarios: CUSTOMER_NAME no longer qualifies, CUST_KEY and CUSTOMER_KEY both qualify (via the suffix leg and the entity+suffix leg respectively), ORDER_DATE no longer qualifies, DATE_KEY still qualifies

computed-only key branch (all serialized equality expressions resolved to non-physical/computed operands, previously an unconditional `continue`): now attempts the same name-match inference before giving up, so a relationship with no serializable physical key can still be recovered by name when the columns exist on both sides

mixed-key branch (skippedComputed > 0, some equality expressions computed and dropped alongside a wired physical subset): unchanged wiring behavior, additionally tags the relationship and its coverage-ledger entry with derivedVia: "serialized", partial: true, droppedConditions: <n>
every relationship object pushed into an element's `relationships` array carries derivedVia: "serialized" | "name-inference"

relationshipCoverage ledger: a `{ serialized, wired, entries: [] }` collector attached to convertTableauToSigma's returned object as `relationshipCoverage` whenever the collection/object-graph branch runs. Every relationship the loop considers — wired or not — pushes exactly one entry (`{ left, right, derivedVia, keyCount }` when wired, or `{ left, right, derivedVia: "unwired", reason, candidates }` when not)

two early `continue` paths (missing first/second end-point, or endpoint object-id(s) that don't resolve to a known element, including both endpoints resolving to the SAME element) push a derivedVia: "unwired" coverage-ledger entry naming the actual cause instead of silently exiting with no record

the computed-only branch's successful-inference path (keys.length === 0, inference ok) records partial: true, droppedConditions: <n> on both the relationship object and its coverage-ledger entry when skippedComputed conditions existed, plus an additional widened-join warning — the same shape the mixed-key/serialized branch already used

KNOWN LIMITATION, NOT FIXED: hasCol/candidateNames trust colIdMap, and every write into colIdMap is a bare assignment with no existence check — if two distinct physical columns on the SAME element normalize to the same key, the later write silently wins and name-inference could resolve to a real-but-WRONG column's id with no signal a collision occurred. Deliberately left unmitigated pending a follow-up that would need to change colIdMap's write sites themselves

_upstream_and_revendor_tasks: Standing vendoring rule: patch upstream and re-vendor; never edit the vendored .mjs in place. When an in-place patch is unavoidable, it lands with its own local_patches entry (commit, summary, upstream_pr) in this file — the hygiene.yml converter-provenance guard rejects any plugins/**/converter/*.mjs diff whose range does not also change the sibling PROVENANCE.json.

TASK 0 (done this re-vendor) — picked up sigma-data-model-mcp PR #118 (source_commit d769bec -> d839036): tableauFormulaToSigma no longer rewrites the CONTENTS of string literals (a literal containing a mapped function name or IN/THEN/ELSE was previously mistranslated; a literal containing THEN could make the IF translator drop an entire branch — a wrong answer, not a cosmetic corruption). This is now the vendored baseline, not a local_patches entry. The two open local_patches entries above were re-applied on top by mechanical diff-replay (build d769bec and d839036 from clean source, diff the OLD build against the previously-shipped bundle to isolate exactly the hand-applied delta, then apply that same diff to the NEW build); 35 of 36 hunks applied verbatim (the rest were harmless bundler path-comment noise from the differently-named local checkout dirs), 1 substantive hunk (the start-of-week literal drop) needed re-implementing against PR #118's new sentinel-masked text and was re-verified live.
TASK 1 — upstream: port each open local_patches entry to source_repo's tableau converter source, one reviewable PR per functional change; set the entry's upstream_pr field when the PR opens.

TASK 2 — re-vendor: after the upstream PR merges, run tools/vendor-converters.sh <checkout> tableau; the source_commit/source_commit_date bump and regeneration of this file are what retire landed local_patches entries.

TASK 3 — guard the unlanded: BOTH regenerators rewrite this file wholesale — tools/vendor-converters.sh (the canonical path) AND the skill-local scripts/dev/vendor-converter.sh (whose header still says to re-run it after converter changes, and which writes a stale schema with no local_patches at all) — so regenerating while any local_patches entry is still open silently drops that patch record; either wait, or re-apply the patch and re-record local_patches (and this task block) in the same commit. Refresh only via tools/vendor-converters.sh.
TASK 4 — prove parity: after any re-vendor, corpus/run-corpus.sh --check and corpus/converter-default-test.sh must stay green before a retirement counts as done.

TASK 5 (new, opened this re-vendor) — the upstream_pr citation on the calc-translation-hotfixes entry (twells89/sigma-data-model-mcp#111, commit 60a0355) does not resolve against current mcp main; confirm whether PR #111 actually landed under a different commit/squash hash, or whether the citation was wrong from the start, and correct or remove it.
